name: Emmeralda
description: Elven courtesan of The Sylph's Embrace -- poised, magnetic, and the finest performer on the Pearl (CHA 18, Seduction 88, Dance 85).
narrative:
Emmeralda is an elven courtesan at The Sylph's Embrace and the most
sought-after performer on the Pearl: a poised, magnetic presence (Dance 85, Sing 80,
Seduction 88) with a following among people who can afford her.

At the campaign's opening she is entirely well, and has an evening booked with a
young nobleman who has paid generously and asked for privacy.

**GM -- what she becomes.** She is Santo's intended vessel. If the binding happens
and she survives it, a lesser pleasure demon stays partly lodged in her: strange
behaviours, bestial voices, and asking after 'Lord Santo.' That makes her the
clearest living proof of what he did -- and, if she recovers enough to stand and
speak, a witness who can **swear over still water**, which in this realm is worth
more than any quantity of parchment -- and -- because an interrupted binding is a
unique case -- the one subject from which a counter-ritual might be devised. Whether
she lives at all depends on who reaches her in the first minutes. None of this is
true yet.

extras.role: Elven courtesan at The Sylph's Embrace who survived Santo di Teufel's botched binding ritual and is partially possessed by a lesser pleasure demon.
extras.possession: Healing interrupted [[santo-di-teufel]]'s ritual before full possession. She suffers strange behaviors, speaks in bestial voices, and occasionally asks for 'Lord Santo.' The demon can surge: brief unnatural strength (treat as STR 16 for one action, claws 1d3) and frightening presence, then she collapses, distraught.
extras.significance: Living evidence of Santo's crime; her interrupted binding is the key to developing a counter-ritual. A potential ally if her possession can be reversed.
extras.magic_tradition: None of her own; the demon-taint is an affliction, not a learned tradition.
extras.source: GM-authored from source lore (The Partially Possessed Courtesan)
